newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt police arrest 26 demonstrating farmers.
newsitem.headline: Egypt police arrest 26 demonstrating farmers.

text.p: Egyptian police on Thursday arrested 26 farmers who allegedly organised a demonstration in southern Egypt in which protesters burnt down two government buildings to protest at a new farm land law.
Security sources said no one was hurt in the incidents which took place in the village of Saft near the town of el-Fashn in Beni Sueif province.
The farmers are angry over the law that will come into effect in October and radically changes the nature of the relationship between land-owners and tenants.
The law scraps many provisions installed by the late socialist president Gamal Abdel-Nasser in the late 1950s to protect tenants.
The existing law makes it almost impossible for land-owners to sell their land without splitting the price with tenants.
Under the new law, land owners can end the lease with their tenants from October and offer the land to a higher bidder, either to another tenant or a buyer.

The detained farmers could face charges of causing public trouble, organising a demonstration and wasting public money. The protesters set fire to the village's agricultural bank and cooperative, the sources said.

Interior Minister Hassan el-Alfi told reporters at the end of a police seminar on Thursday that the government would not change its mind about the new law and that security forces would deal firmly with any trouble.
The government has said it would provide reclaimed land to tenants who lose leases once the law comes into effect.

Opponents of the law have brushed this aside, saying there would not be enough land for all and that the formerly desert land would need a lot of work to become as fertile as the land they used to tend.
